name: store_scatter
kind: attribution and service-axis validation; no workload-based fitting
question: Does a store's SMSP issue interval depend on instruction width or on the sectors/lines generated by its lane addresses? The existing lsu_accept v5 only used contiguous addresses, confounding width_bytes 4/8/16 with sector_count 4/8/16. load_after_stores engine replay gives K=32 extra 210/132 cycles for same/other warp versus hardware 974-976/943; its 32-sector U16 stores issue mostly 23 cycles apart under the installed sector_count leaf.
probe: probe.cu reuses lsu_accept's store_queue kernel without changing its timing body. Widths 2/4/8/16 bytes, lane strides width/32/128 bytes, W=1/2 warps; clock-only control. Twenty-four stores per window on distinct pointer registers. Runs a/b, 16 launches and 65 repetitions, repetition zero discarded. Each (request,warp) owns 8192 bytes, all addresses aligned, no alias across requests or warps.

controls.sass: Five k_cell kernels, 25 CLOCKLO reads, exactly one STG of the declared width between neighboring reads (zero for control), 24 distinct address registers, no extra memory/barrier/branch in the window. Original checker reused with explicit U16 variant.
controls.timing: Contiguous widths 4/8/16 should reproduce lsu_accept v5 intervals 3/6/23 within max(2 cycles,15%). Runs a/b first-issue estimates should agree within max(2 cycles,10%). Failures are reported and investigated, not automatically reclassified as valid.
controls.scope: W=1 and W=2 occupy different SMSPs. Early gaps separate local issue from later finite-buffer backpressure; all 24 gaps are retained so an early knee cannot be hidden.

derivation: For each run and cell, retain per-gap sample medians. c0 is the clock-only W=1 median of gaps 2..24. Early issue estimate I(width,stride,W) = median of gap medians 2..4 minus (c0-1), clamped only to zero for reporting. Also report each of the 24 gap medians and the tail median (17..24); do not infer a service leaf from a backpressured tail.

outcomes_before_data.width: If early issue estimates at fixed width agree across strides and W within max(2 cycles,15%), while different widths retain their separation, the installed sector_count axis is not supported. Candidate change: existing storage.global.store_issue cycles keyed by capture width_bytes, with measured points including width 2; same per-SMSP gate, no new queue.
outcomes_before_data.geometry: If early estimates systematically change with stride at fixed width beyond that tolerance, report width/sector_count/cache_line_count jointly; no automatic installation or extrapolation. A subsequent addendum must specify the supported mechanism before any engine or leaf change.
outcomes_before_data.none: If controls or first-window independence fail, report the SASS/timing cause and repair the probe before installing anything.

prediction: Any candidate must replay the existing load_after_stores capture through the engine and report same/other K=0/8/32 deltas against the frozen r1 hardware data, plus explain saturation as a separate queue question. Hardware's actual clock window contains seven dependent loads: ptxas moved the eighth load after the closing clock; replay measures the same two PCs and does not divide by eight.
validation: Only full-gpu accuracy is the optimization gate per user's current instruction: both architectures 500 cases with r16's exact cases, placement and hardware reference. Keep CTest and targeted converter/tree correctness tests; do not claim success with failures or reduced coverage. Target each architecture MAPE<5%, P90 absolute relative error<10%.
not_allowed: No family/case/shape-specific timing, no tuning a measured value to the full-gpu error, no treating instrumented probe output as uninstrumented hardware timing. Any post-data protocol adjustment must be labelled.

addenda.text: Both devices passed the five-kernel SASS check and contiguous controls. Early issue intervals at widths 2/4/8/16 B are exactly 3/3/6/23 cycles across all three strides, W=1/2 and both runs. Thus the declared width outcome holds without changing any threshold. Install the existing per-SMSP store issue mechanism on capture width_bytes with points [2,3],[4,3],[8,6],[16,23]. Keep the existing port service, rule S, R1 and orders_loads unchanged. Late gaps show geometry-dependent buffering/service and remain a separate investigation. The load_after_stores replay and full-gpu validation are still pending at this point.
